text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make the code easier to read, understand, and maintain. Developers often refactor to remove duplication, simplify complex logic, or give variables clearer names. It is important to remember that refactoring should not change the program's behavior, so tests are essential. Over time, poorly written code creates technical debt, which makes future changes slower and riskier. By refactoring regularly, teams keep their code clean and healthy, reduce technical debt, and make it easier for everyone to work on the project.
